sample: One of the 10 instances (LLF-02 to 11) that are methods of the same class Config (line 1255 of argos_ai_adventure.py), in two patterns: 4 setters that serialize nested lists with ','.join(map(lambda ...)) and 6 getters that undo it with split(','). By the function rule, each method is an instance; recorded as a limitation.
removed_from_original: lines 1 to 3, module docstring: names the game and is not used by the snippet.
lines 5 to 13, imports argparse, sys, pathlib, time, random, math, json and importlib: not used by the snippet.

the other methods of the Config class (load_config, save_config, persist_config, the other get_config_* and set_config_*): outside the snippet. Taking the whole class would put in the scaffolding the other 9 LLF detections of the class, which are instances of their own.
the other classes (GameData, Node, World, Player, Logger etc.), the __main__ block and main(): outside the snippet; GameData also reads game_data.json from disk when the module is imported.
scaffolding: run(text): creates Config, stores text in the 'world' section, key 'regions', calls the method and passes the result through _materialize.

_materialize(value): the method returns nested, lazy map iterators; the scaffolding turns them into lists so the test can compare them. Text stays text, and what is not iterable (number, bool) stays as it is.
Checked: Pysmell only flags the method; nothing in the scaffolding.
pinned_behavior: typical: each item goes through int and comes back wrapped in three one-element lists ('3,-1,+7' becomes [[[[3]]], [[[-1]]], [[[7]]]]). Compared by repr, to pin the int type.
edge: int accepts surrounding spaces and underscores ('1_000' becomes 1000); zero.
invalid: an item with a decimal point ('3.5') raises ValueError.
not_pinned_on_purpose: Return type: the original returns nested map iterators; since run turns everything into lists, returning lists, tuples or generators also passes.

When the error happens: in the original, an error inside the inner lambdas only shows up when the result is iterated; run iterates everything, so the test does not tell an error in the call from an error in the consumption.
Missing section or key (KeyError): run always stores the key before reading it.
